note: ADR-0037 / PRD decision 40.5 — the agent domain's first cut at the assembled edge. Four tools today, all GET, because that is what binds: `bind.py` derives a tool's argument schema from its route's OpenAPI `parameters`, and every workspace WRITE route here (`PUT /api/workspace/file`, `POST /api/workspace/entity`, `POST /api/claims`, `POST /api/workspace/shared/new`, `POST /api/workspace/purpose`) takes a single JSON-body parameter (`body: dict = Body(...)` or a Pydantic model), which FastAPI publishes under `requestBody`, not `parameters` — confirmed by dumping this app's own `openapi()`. Declaring them as tools today would either fail `bind.py`'s verification outright or, left undeclared, publish a schema with zero arguments and no way to pass `kind`/`name`/`facts`/etc — 'the worst reply available' by this codebase's own words in register.py, a tool an agent can call and be told it worked while nothing happened. Same class of gap flows' own manifest already lives with (`flows_submit`/`flow_lifecycle` are real FLOWS_API routes, absent from core/flows/mcp.tools.v1.json for the identical reason). Tracked, with the full tool-by-tool breakdown, at the issue this manifest shipped with.

tools.name: workspace_tree
tools.note: The file listing for the caller's own workspace, or one of their shared workspaces named by `slug`. `hidden` includes dotfiles.

tools.name: workspace_read
tools.note: Read one file's content by its relative path. `slug` selects a shared workspace; omitted, it is the caller's own.

tools.name: workspace_purpose
tools.note: Reads the one-line PURPOSE a workspace carries. The SET side (`POST /api/workspace/purpose`) is a `WorkspacePurposeBody` JSON-body route and is not yet bindable — see the manifest-level note above.
